description: Intersect two bounded simple polygons using linked entry/exit crossings and emit canonical exact-rational boundary rings.

source.title: Weiler-Atherton polygon clipping
source.discovery_scope: RosettaCodeData supplies title discovery only. The bounded input, general-position restrictions, exact rational framing, traversal tie rule, and canonical output are original benchmark choices.

input.orientation: Both polygons must be strictly counterclockwise.
input.geometry_rules: Each input is simple, has distinct vertices and no collinear consecutive edges. Cross-polygon intersections must be proper interior edge crossings; boundary contacts, shared/overlapping edges, and endpoint intersections are invalid. Collinear cross-polygon edge pairs with disjoint segments are allowed.

output.rational_coordinates: Each fraction is reduced, has positive denominator, and represents an exact boundary coordinate.
output.canonicalization: Each ring follows the intersection boundary with its interior on the left. Rotate each ring so its lexicographically least rational point is first, then sort rings lexicographically by their point sequences.

contract.primary_method: Insert all proper edge intersections in boundary order into both cyclic polygon lists. Label each crossing by the local inside/outside transition. Start at the least unvisited entry crossing on polygon A, follow A to an exit, switch to the paired crossing on B, and continue alternating until the start is reached. If there are no crossings, return the contained polygon or an empty result.
contract.independent_method: Split every directed input edge at all proper crossings, retain fragments whose exact rational midpoint lies inside the other polygon, then join directed fragments by exact endpoint equality into closed rings.
contract.tie_rule: Crossings are ordered by input polygon edge index and increasing segment parameter. Entry starts use polygon-A list order. These rules determinize equivalent boundary walks; canonicalization removes start-point and ring-order variation.

workspace.meaning: Covers bounded edge events, interleaved boundary nodes, exact rational points, ring staging, and output words. Caller-owned input and output buffers are excluded.

complexity.primary_time: O(n_a*n_b + k*(n_a+n_b+k)) with k proper crossings, n_a,n_b<=6
complexity.independent_reference_time: O(n_a*n_b + v^2) with v<=48 boundary vertices
